subject: Advanced glycation end products
context: Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) are a heterogeneous, complex group of compounds that are formed mainly via the Maillard reaction.

subject: Maillard reaction
context: The Maillard reaction occurs when reducing sugar reacts in a non-enzymatic way with amino acids in proteins, lipids or DNA.

subject: Schiff base
context: First, glucose attaches to a free amino acid (mainly lysine and arginine) of a protein, lipid or DNA, in a non–enzymatic way to form a Schiff base.

subject: Amadori products
context: During the second phase, the Schiff base undergoes chemical rearrangement over a period of days and form Amadori products (also known as early glycation products).

subject: AGEs
context: They are very stable, and accumulate inside and outside the cells and interfere with protein function

subject: AGE-RAGE interaction
context: The interaction of AGEs with the receptor RAGE triggers the activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs) and the phosphatidylinositol-3 kinase (PI3-K) pathways that will lead to the activation of the transcription factor NF-κB

subject: NF-κB
context: After activation, NF-κB translocates to the nucleus where it will activate the transcription of genes for cytokines... such as tumor necrosis factor α (TNFα)

subject: NF-κB
context: After activation, NF-κB translocates to the nucleus where it will activate the transcription of genes for cytokines... such as interleukin 6 (Il-6)

subject: AGE-RAGE interaction
context: In addition, AGE-RAGE interaction activates NAD(P)H oxidase (a complex of enzymes which produces superoxide)

subject: NAD(P)H oxidase
context: The sudden increase in oxidative stress by NAD(P)H oxidase in response to AGE-RAGE interaction will also activate NF-κB

subject: AGEs
context: Accumulation of AGEs has been found in healthy aging persons... but it is also associated with atherosclerosis, Alzheimer’s disease...
